solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Part A?

definitions.meaning: an actor's part or role in a play
the letter A is one written symbol of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A cryptic label pointing at the first section of something, Part A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part A' looks like a section heading; split it into two meanings: a role in a play, and a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A role played on stage and a letter of the alphabet are both called by this one word.

clue.text: Men's leather overalls

definitions.meaning: leather leggings worn by cowboys over trousers

explanation.definitionFit: Informal British for blokes, and also leather leggings worn over trousers by riders.

clue.text: From Diana to Misty, one studies bodies

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the run of words

explanation.surface: A person examining a sequence of figures from one woman to another.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in anatomy studies the structure of bodies.

clue.text: Costs of entering commercial ventures?

parts.note: a commercial is an advert, an ad
missions are undertakings or ventures

explanation.surface: The expense of starting business enterprises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial ventures' reads as one business phrase, but the two words do separate jobs; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Admissions are entrance fees, the charges paid to get into a venue.

clue.text: Plant husband chucked out of house with energy

indicators.note: chucked out means removed from the word

parts.note: a theatre is a house, as in 'full house'
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A spouse is thrown out of the home with great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: THEATRE loses H to give TEATRE, then E is added.
explanation.definitionFit: The tea tree is an Australian shrub whose oil is used in medicine.

clue.text: Double entendre ITV cut after about 11?

indicators.note: the pun and the trimmed channel name come after the word for about

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a pun is a play on two meanings

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: ITV is a British commercial television channel

explanation.surface: A TV channel edits out a risqué joke around eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: ITV is a UK broadcaster; cut it to IT. '11' looks like a time of night but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A number written entirely with ones, like eleven or 111, is called by this mathematical term.

clue.text: Simple singer curtly bows to Irish crowd

indicators.note: said curtly, the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a bass is a singer with the lowest male voice

indicators.note: the first letters of the two words come forward and bow, starting each word

explanation.surface: An unsophisticated vocalist gives a brief bow to an audience in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtly' cuts the last letter from BASS, leaving BAS; then the heads of 'Irish' and 'crowd' give I and C.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and simple are synonyms describing something plain and uncomplicated.

clue.text: I go on live to be probed by old Republican

indicators.note: something probed has another thing poked into it

parts.note: to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: A speaker plans to keep living even under investigation by an elderly US politician.
explanation.walkthrough: O + R go inside BE. 'I go on' is the answer speaking: a tedious person goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: A tedious person who talks at length is said to go on and on.

clue.text: Polish function that hotel puts on

indicators.note: the hotel letter is put onto the inside of the function, worn within it

parts.note: sine is a trigonometric function
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel lays on a smart event, needing everything polished.
explanation.walkthrough: H goes inside SINE. 'Polish' looks like the nationality but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine shoes is to polish them until they gleam.

clue.text: Shocked member of government spoke profanely

parts.note: Con is short for a Conservative, the governing party when this appeared
cussed means swore

explanation.surface: A minister was so startled that they swore.
explanation.definitionFit: Concussed means dazed by a blow to the head, a physical form of being shocked.

clue.text: A gun loaded with bit of lead creates panic

indicators.note: a gun loaded with something holds it inside, so the letters go within

parts.note: an arm is a weapon such as a gun

indicators.note: a bit of the word lead is just its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone waving a gun stuffed with lead bullets causes terror.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside A + ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarm is a noun for sudden fear or fright, a close synonym of panic.

clue.text: Slur like individual that one's punched

parts.note: as means like, in the same way as

indicators.note: a person who has been punched has something driven into them, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an individual is a person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An insult is compared to someone who has been hit.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspersion is a damaging remark about someone's character, much like a slur.

clue.text: He's sorting out one that's been tied up?

indicators.note: letters put out of their order are scrambled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A man is busy untangling something that had been bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'out' alone signals the rearrangement of all ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A lace for footwear is tied up in a knot or bow, so it is a cryptic description of one.

clue.text: Lover's from London borough by the sound of it

indicators.note: tells the solver the entry is a word pronounced like another

parts.note: Bow is a district of East London

explanation.surface: A sweetheart comes from a part of London, judging by the accent.
explanation.walkthrough: BOW, a district in London's East End, is pronounced the same as the French-derived word for a boyfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is an old-fashioned word for a boyfriend or male admirer.

clue.text: Radio broadcast on artists close to Jagger

indicators.note: broadcast seeds are scattered, so the letters are scattered too
the close of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A radio show transmits a programme about performers near Mick Jagger.
explanation.walkthrough: ON + ARTISTS + R (end of Jagger) are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A transistor was the everyday name for a small portable radio set.

clue.text: When one over the eight, one's drunk and silly

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
I is the Roman numeral for one
one more than eight is nine

explanation.surface: Someone who has had one too many is drunk and foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for being slightly drunk, so 'one's drunk' merely restates the surface; the letters come from 'When', 'one' and 'over the eight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means foolish like a donkey, a strong synonym for silly.

clue.text: Trams made to run here?

indicators.note: letters made to run are set loose into a new order

explanation.surface: A city where trams were built to operate.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as a definition: the Dutch capital is known for its trams.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch capital has an extensive tram network running through its streets.

clue.text: Clothing lines

definitions.meaning: slang for clothes, as in 'nice outfit'
fine strands of cotton or yarn

explanation.definitionFit: Slang uses this word for garments, and the same word means thin strands of yarn.

clue.text: It could keep the shock from one's eyes

definitions.text: It could keep the shock from one's eyes

parts.words: It could keep the shock from one's eyes
parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and this headband holds it back off the face

explanation.surface: Something that protects you from witnessing a horrifying sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' suggests a fright, but it is a shock of hair; the item is a hairband like the one in Alice in Wonderland illustrations.
explanation.definitionFit: A wide headband holds a mop of hair back from the forehead and eyes.

clue.text: Bag lined with brown bit of inlay is wicked

indicators.note: a bag lined with something holds it on the inside

parts.note: a sac is a baglike pouch
tan is a light brown

indicators.note: a bit of inlay is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A handbag with a brown inlaid lining is described as evil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lined with' puts the brown and the inlay's first letter inside the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means devilish, so it describes something extremely evil.

clue.text: Eccentric in charge withholding ace of hearts

parts.note: a card is an eccentric, amusing person

indicators.note: something withheld is held within

parts.note: A is short for ace in cards

explanation.surface: A wacky person in authority keeps back the ace of hearts in a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ace of hearts' looks like one playing card, but 'of hearts' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardiac is the medical adjective relating to the heart.

clue.text: Sugar-coated advice at last welcomed by Frank

indicators.note: something welcomed by a host is taken in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: candid means frank or open

indicators.note: points to the closing letter of advice

explanation.surface: An honest person accepts some advice at the end of a talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Candied fruit is coated or preserved in sugar.

clue.text: Daily and what it is without Page Three?

definitions.meaning: a daily is a domestic help who comes in each day

definitions.text: what it is without Page Three?
definitions.meaning: a tabloid would be less smutty without its topless pin-up

explanation.surface: A newspaper and how it would look without its notorious feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Page Three was The Sun newspaper's daily photo of a topless model; 'Daily' looks like a newspaper but is a cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: A housekeeper who comes daily, and the comparative of tidy or less smutty.

clue.text: Make wish to see leader given the boot

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and giving it the boot kicks it out

parts.note: to yearn is to wish or long for

explanation.surface: Someone wishes to see their boss sacked.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, so the two verbs are synonyms here.

clue.text: The Queen's upset by university guidelines

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina
MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Her Majesty is annoyed by a college's rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A remit is the set of terms or instructions defining a task, much like guidelines.

clue.text: Weird presences around one could engender this

definitions.text: Weird presences around one could engender this

indicators.note: the presences are placed around the letter for one
weird means strange, so the letters are put into a strange new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Ghostly presences surrounding a person would give them an eerie feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside PRESENCES and the whole is rearranged; read as a whole, the clue also describes the feeling ghosts produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie ghostly presences around someone produce a spooky, unsettling feeling.

clue.text: Composer that's after soprano and a tenor

indicators.note: that is placed after the other letters

parts.note: ie is short for id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: A musician who follows a soprano and a tenor on a programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Erik Satie was a French composer famous for the Gymnopédies.

clue.text: Song about daughter titled "Woman"

indicators.note: the song wraps about the letter

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A tune about a girl bears the title 'Woman'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'titled' looks like part of the song's name but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A noblewoman with a title is styled with this word, as is any polite woman.

clue.text: Flipping angry people can be hell

indicators.note: flipping a word turns it backwards

parts.note: mad means angry
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Annoyed people can be infuriating, a cry of exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British expletive but it reverses MAD to DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Damnation is eternal punishment in hell, so it stands for hell itself.

clue.text: Like to tuck into drink after this?

definitions.text: Like to tuck into drink after this?

indicators.note: something tucked into a word is placed inside it

parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits
as means like

explanation.surface: Wanting to dig into a drink after a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue also describes the custom of raising glasses and drinking once the speech of good wishes is made.
explanation.definitionFit: At a celebration a speech of good wishes is made, and everyone then drinks.

clue.text: Around heads of the EU, the PM is friendly

indicators.note: the PM's name goes around the letters

parts.note: Theresa May was the UK Prime Minister when this puzzle appeared

indicators.note: the heads of the two words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Among European Union leaders, the British Prime Minister is on good terms.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was Britain's Prime Minister during the 2019 Brexit talks, when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey is informal British for sociable and pally.

clue.text: Magazine about game birds with no wings

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outermost letters, removed here

parts.note: partridges are birds shot for sport

explanation.surface: A periodical writes about shooting birds with damaged wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no wings' strips P and S from PARTRIDGES, leaving ARTRIDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine in a gun holds the cartridges, and a cartridge is itself a holder of film or ink, so both are containers loaded into a device.
